excerpt: Pindrop detects voice fraud and audio deepfakes in phone calls, contact centres and virtual meetings. It raised $100 million in debt in 2024. What it does and alternatives.
content:
Pindrop makes voice security software. It analyses the audio, device and network signals in a phone call to authenticate genuine callers and flag fraudsters, mainly for companies with large contact centres. As voice cloning has spread, it has focused on deepfake detection: its Pindrop Pulse product identifies synthetic or AI-generated voices in real time, and its website now pitches deepfake defence for calls, virtual meetings and contact centres.

In July 2024 Pindrop announced $100 million in debt financing from Hercules Capital to develop its audio, voice and AI technology, SiliconANGLE and SecurityWeek reported. According to its announcement, the company had raised $218.3 million in venture equity since it was founded in 2011. It also said it had analysed 5.3 billion calls, helped prevent $2 billion in fraud losses and detected 104 million spoofed calls, and that contact centre fraud had risen 60% in two years; these are the company's own figures. Alongside Pulse it launched a deepfake warranty that reimburses eligible customers if its products miss a deepfake or synthetic-voice fraud.

Pindrop does not publish prices; it sells to enterprises through its sales team. It suits organisations that verify customers over the phone, while smaller companies usually rely on the fraud tools in their telephony provider. It competes with voice biometrics and fraud products from Nuance (Microsoft) and NICE, and with newer deepfake detection startups such as Reality Defender.

We have not used Pindrop for this page. It brings together Pindrop's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
